topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Arithmetic and Geometry

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Infinite Staircase
lecture_lines: Imagine jumping across blocks that shrink by half.
An infinite sum can reach a finite destination.
This is the foundation of the Zeta function.
animations: step1
step2
step3

sections.title: Defining the Zeta Function ζ(s)
lecture_lines: Define the Zeta function as an infinite sum.
Each term is the reciprocal of n raised to s.
The variable s controls how fast terms shrink.
Adjusting the lever s changes the series' behavior.
Watch how the sum evolves as s increases.
animations: Display the formula ζ(s) = Σ (1/n^s) in the center, color #ADD8E6.
Highlight the 's' exponent in the denominator with a yellow #FFFF00 glowing effect.
Transform the formula into its expanded form: 1 + 1/2^s + 1/3^s +..., keeping the 's' highlighted in yellow #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Convergence Boundary (s > 1)
lecture_lines: At s equals one, the sum grows forever.
This boundary separates divergence from convergence.
For s greater than one, the sum stays finite.
animations: Display 's = 1' next to a vertical bar that grows upwards off-screen, color shifting from #FFFFFF to #FF0000.
Display 's = 1.1' next to a second vertical bar that grows but decelerates and stops at a finite height, color #00FF00.
A semi-transparent blue rectangle #ADD8E6 covers the area where s > 1, labeled 'Convergence Zone'.

sections.title: The Basel Problem: Geometry in Numbers
lecture_lines: At s equals two, something surprising happens.
The sum of squared reciprocals equals pi squared over six.
Integers and circles are connected through this function.
animations: Write ζ(2) = 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 +... in #FFFFFF at the top of the screen.
Transform the entire sum into the value π²/6 in bright yellow #FFFF00.
Draw a circle with radius 1 in #ADD8E6 and highlight its circumference to evoke geometry.
Show the formula for circle area (πr²) appearing next to the zeta value, highlighting the π symbol.
The π in π²/6 and the π in the circle formula flash in sync using white #FFFFFF to show the connection.

sections.title: Analytic Continuation: Stretching the Domain
lecture_lines: Beyond s equals one, the sum formula fails.
We stretch the function across the complex plane.
This analytic continuation reveals values like zeta negative one.
animations: Show a coordinate grid representing the complex plane (Real and Imaginary axes) in #555555.
Color the region to the right of Re(s)=1 in light blue #ADD8E6.
Display the original Zeta sum formula over this blue region.
Animate a 'smooth expansion' where the color spreads from the blue region to cover the entire plane, turning #00FF00.
Highlight the point (-1, 0) and display ζ(-1) = -1/12 in #FFFFFF nearby.

sections.title: The Golden Link: Euler Product Formula
lecture_lines: Zeta bridges addition and the mystery of primes.
Euler found a product formula over all prime numbers.
Every natural number is built from prime factors.
This identity is the DNA of number theory.
The function encodes the distribution of all primes.
animations: Position the sum Σ (1/n^s) on the left and the product Π (1/(1-p⁻ˢ)) on the right in #FFFFFF.
Draw a central box labeled 'Euler Sieve' in gold #FFD700.
Animate integers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... moving from the left into the sieve box.
Composite numbers (4, 6, 8...) disappear inside; prime numbers (2, 3, 5...) exit to the right product side.
The equals sign between the sum and the product grows and flashes in #FFFFFF to emphasize the identity.

sections.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Million Dollar Line
lecture_lines: Zeros of the function hold a million-dollar secret.
Trivial zeros are easy to find on the negative axis.
Riemann conjectured all others lie on the critical line.
This line is at the real part of one-half.
Proving this would unlock the pattern of primes.
animations: Draw the complex plane focusing on the strip between Re(s)=0 and Re(s)=1, shaded in #333333.
Draw a bold vertical line at Re(s)=0.5 in red #FF0000, labeled 'Critical Line'.
Animate several small points (zeros) appearing one by one along the red line, each pulsing with yellow #FFFF00.
